data.title: Clarity Act preliminary vote falls short in Senate amid ethics fight over Trump’s crypto wealth
data.description:
An initial vote to try to push the Clarity Act closer to becoming law fell flat amid Democratic opposition to President Donald Trump's vast crypto wealth.

On Tuesday, the U.S. Senate failed to advance the bill without the necessary 60 votes.

Sen. Cynthia Lummis, R-Wyo., the bill’s lead architect, had called the moment “now or never" ahead of the cloture vote, in a post on X.

The measure would create the first comprehensive federal framework for the crypto industry. Over the past year, though, it has been battered by a still-unresolved fight between banks and crypto firms over stablecoins, and by lingering concerns about illicit finance.

Ahead of the vote, Senate Republicans released a revised version of the Clarity Act that included some new language for "non-decentralized finance protocols," but did little to change one area that has been one of Democrats' biggest concerns — ethics. Trump's crypto wealth has grown to hundreds of millions of dollars linked to World Liberty Financial and his TRUMP memecoin.

Republicans, led by Sen. Lummis, later released new text that gives state attorneys general some leeway in enforcing the ethics provisions by allowing them to sue crypto exchanges and the Justice Department, and says that public officials have to divest "significant financial interest" or put those in a blind trust. But Democrats have said that provision is not enforceable given that the Justice Department would decide whether to bring an enforcement action against the president.

On Monday night, Senate Democrats prepared the counteroffer, asking to amend the ethics provision to address Trump's growing crypto profits, specifically by broadening ethics restrictions to address Trump's vast crypto wealth, including his children, and requiring officials with a "very large interest in a crypto company to sell it," not just put it in a blind trust, according to reporting from Politico. But Lummis later shut down that offer.

With the failure of Tuesday's vote, it is unclear how the bill moves forward. Time is squeezed ahead of midterm elections in November as lawmakers go on recess and focus turns to campaigning. The Senate could decide to hold another procedural vote if there is enough floor time.

If the Senate passed the bill, the House would need to vote on it as well, which wouldn't be until after the November elections since they cancelled their last two weeks of September.

Meanwhile, the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission have begun moving forward with rulemaking, but the Clarity Act is viewed as essential because it gives more permanency to regulatory frameworks.

On Monday, SEC Chair Paul Atkins said lawmakers should advance the Clarity Act, but said his agency was moving onward.

"But let me be equally clear: with or without that legislation, this Administration will deliver for American investors and technological innovators—which is immensely important to our markets and to those who participate in them," Atkins said at a Solana Policy Institute event. "Promises were made, and they will be kept."

data.title: West Fraser raised at Raymond James as 'housing recovery not necessary to buy the trees'
data.description:
West Fraser Timber gains 2.1% in Tuesday's trading as Raymond James upgraded the wood products company to Outperform from Market Perform with an $85 price target, which also raised Interfor and Canfor to Strong Buy, saying a U.S. housing recovery is "not necessary to buy the trees."

After four years of depressed U.S. housing, repair, and renovation activity, Raymond James analyst Daryl Swetlishoff said the supply side "has finally done the heavy lifting to improve balance in North American lumber markets," Canadian shipments have fallen to record lows, capacity has permanently exited the system, and European lumber imports have fallen sharply.

Despite cyclical and seasonal demand headwinds, 2026 results approached "what we consider mid-cycle profitability with our refreshed 3Q26 estimates not too far behind," the analyst wrote.

With lumber equities still trading at or below tangible book value, Swetlishoff said a U.S. housing recovery is not currently priced in the stocks, but the analyst "could see ~30% higher benchmark lumber pricing, translating to 100%-300% theoretical equity upside... hence, we see a compelling asymmetric setup with meaningful upside available before underwriting any macro improvement."

"We recommend investors build full positions now as we head into the 2026-27 seasonal trade," the analyst said.

data.title: CBOT soybeans end higher as soymeal surges on monthly US crush data
data.description:
Chicago Board of Trade soybean futures ended higher on Tuesday as soymeal futures surged more than 2% after a monthly industry report showed a smaller-than-expected soybean crushing pace in August, traders said.

  • A jump in crude oil prices tied to supply disruptions in the Middle East lent additional support to soybeans and corn, both of which are used in the production of biofuels.

  • CBOT November soybeans (SX26) settled up 14-1/2 cents, or 1.1%, at $13.18-3/4 per bushel.

  • CBOT December soymeal (SMZ26) ended up $9.20, or 2.6%, at $365.40 per ton. All contract months other than most-active December set life-of-contract highs.

  • CBOT December soyoil rose 0.16 cent, or 0.2%, to finish at 70.35 cents per pound.

  • The National Oilseed Processors Association said its members crushed 205.456 million bushels of soybeans in August, an 11-month low, and soyoil stocks thinned to the lowest level since November 2024.

  • Brazilian crop agency Conab forecast the country's 2026/27 soybean production at 181.64 million metric tons, up 0.7% from the previous year but below the U.S. Department of Agriculture's current forecast for Brazil of 186 million tons.

  • Harvesting was underway in the U.S. Midwest, although heavy rains were stalling field work in parts of Iowa.

  • The USDA on Monday reported harvest progress at 8% for corn and 6% for soybeans, ahead of their respective five-year averages of 6% and 3%.

data.title: New Mexico Cybersecurity Firm “CyberSandia” Discusses Public Sector Cyberthreats with State Cybersecurity Leaders
data.description:
CyberSandia, a New Mexico-based cybersecurity firm owned by TAC Security, brought together state cybersecurity leaders and public sector professionals for a discussion on evolving cyberthreats and strengthening the security of government services.

The gathering was addressed by Trishneet Arora, Founder & CEO of TAC Security, and Hector Balderas, former Attorney General of New Mexico and a member of TAC Security’s U.S. Board of Directors. Bruce Oakeley, Director of CyberSandia, and Aaron Frankel, Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) of CyberSandia, also shared their perspectives on cybersecurity challenges facing public sector organizations.

The engagement provided a forum for government and cybersecurity leaders to exchange views on protecting public systems, strengthening preparedness and making cybersecurity capabilities more accessible to agencies.

Trishneet Arora, Founder & CEO of TAC Security, said: “Cybersecurity in the public sector is ultimately about protecting people—their information, the services they depend on and their trust in government. Through CyberSandia, we are bringing TAC Security’s global expertise closer to New Mexico’s agencies. Our focus is to help public sector leaders identify risk, prioritize action and access the capabilities they need to build stronger, more resilient digital services.”

Trishneet Arora reflected on TAC Security’s deep connection with New Mexico, where the company began its U.S. journey in Albuquerque in 2018 before growing into a global cybersecurity leader.

Hector Balderas, former Attorney General of New Mexico and a member of TAC Security’s U.S. Board of Directors, said: “Protecting New Mexico’s digital infrastructure requires collaboration between government leaders and cybersecurity professionals who understand the responsibilities of public service. This engagement is an opportunity to strengthen that collaboration and support agencies working to safeguard our communities.”

CyberSandia operates as Sandia IT & Cybersecurity Services, LLC and holds a State of New Mexico Contract Vehicle for IT Professional Services. This established procurement pathway helps streamline contracting, reduce administrative complexity and facilitate access to cost-effective IT and cybersecurity products and services for the State of New Mexico and eligible government agencies.

Backed by TAC Security, which reports ranking among the world’s five largest vulnerability management and application security companies, CyberSandia aims to strengthen its role as a trusted cybersecurity partner to New Mexico’s public sector.

data.title: Canada Looks to Lure New Investment With Aggressive, Broad Tax Writeoff Terms — Update
data.description:
By Robb M. Stewart and Paul Vieira

Canada is implementing a tax change tied to the accelerated write off of capital equipment that attempts to move the country toward Prime Minister Mark Carney's goal of attracting nearly $1 trillion of new investment.

Lobbying groups for Canadian companies applauded the decision and said it could set the stage for an investment renaissance. Economists and public-policy analysts dubbed this the most substantial change to Canada's tax code in decades, and helps Canada compete following President Trump's tax revamp introduced last year.

Carney's announcement on Tuesday is aimed at strengthening Canada's tax competitiveness and encouraging investment at a time when Canada is confronted with a toughened trade environment and hefty tariffs on key exports to the U.S. Officials said the proposed change will improve productivity and strengthen the economy.

Dubbed the productivity-mega deduction, the government said it will allow for the immediate expensing of a broad-based range of depreciable property on a permanent basis. This would allow businesses to fully write off the cost of an investment in the year that it becomes available for use.

"Simply, your investment dollars will go a lot further in Canada than anywhere else in the advanced world," Carney told an audience at an investment summit in Toronto, where he hopes to match some of the world's biggest investors with Canadian companies pitching shovel-ready projects.

The big change, analysts said, is that officials are expanding the types of assets eligible for the accelerated writeoff. The writeoff was previously limited to assets in the manufacturing sector. That deduction can now be applied more broadly, to the energy and mining sectors and broadband for instance, thereby covering about two-thirds of all capital investment, officials said.

"This is a measure that helps address the single largest economic challenge Canada faces currently--productivity," said Trevor Tombe, an economics professor at the University of Calgary, adding business investment is the most important driver of productivity. Levels of productivity and business investment have been so lackluster that it prompted a senior Bank of Canada official in 2024 to declare the economic challenges a national emergency.

Carney said the expensing changes will position Canada as a tax-competitive leader for new investment, by offering the lowest marginal effective tax rate among Group of Seven nations. In charts accompanying his announcement, Carney said Canada's marginal effective tax rate--or the level of taxation from all levels of government on every additional dollar of capital spending--will now be less than half the U.S. rate, and roughly one-third of the average for Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development countries.

"We are making it cheaper to invest," the prime minister said. At a press conference, he said the government needed to offer immediate incentives to investors to accomplish its goal of building new trade corridors and resource projects that are necessary to restore economic resiliency.

"We need a clear advantage. We have a clear advantage now," Carney said.

Business Council of Canada chief executive Goldy Hyder said his group was pushing for such a move to be included in the government's upcoming 2026 budget plan. The measure "will help catalyze investment in Canada's capital infrastructure," said Hyder, who represents CEOs from the country's biggest corporations.

Candace Laing, head of Canadian Chamber of Commerce, said she expects the measure to "unlock investment and create jobs...The permanency of this deduction at these levels will draw the attention and interest of investors in Canada for longer than any investment summit could last."

The government estimates the incremental cost of the measure to be about C$36 billion, about $25.67 billion U.S., across five years from the 2026-27 fiscal year. Officials estimate the tax change could increase economic output by C$22 billion annually.

data.title: US attorney general says probes handled by ex-prosecutor DiGenova will continue
data.description:
U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche said on Tuesday that any probes that former federal prosecutor Joseph DiGenova had been handling would continue.

DiGenova, who oversaw a wide-ranging probe into past investigations of President Donald Trump, resigned last week.

"I very much appreciate the work that he did for us and for the administration," Blanche told reporters at the White house. "Any investigations that he's working on, of course, continue like they do, like any investigation does when somebody leaves, and we're not going to slow down just because somebody leaves."

DiGenova ​joined the Justice Department in April to take over the Florida-based investigation that has been scrutinizing several of Trump’s foes and has sought to establish that the president was the victim of a long-running criminal conspiracy.

The investigation has ​examined the 2017 U.S. intelligence finding that Russia sought to boost Trump’s first presidential campaign in 2016, as ​well as more recent investigations by former Special Counsel Jack Smith that probed Trump’s retention of classified documents at his Mar-a-Lago resort and his attempts to overturn his 2020 election defeat. The investigation has so far not resulted in any criminal charges.

DiGenova, a Trump ally, did not provide a reason for his resignation.

data.title: Why This Taser Maker's Stock Is Second-Worst in the S&P 500 — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Ty Roush

Shares of Axon Enterprise declined sharply Tuesday and were the worst performers in the S&P 500 after the Taser maker announced plans to raise $1 billion, and potentially more, in debt.

Investors reacted negatively to the plan as shares fell 8.6%, their worst session since Aug. 7,. The stock has fallen 21% this year.

Axon disclosed a proposed offering of $1 billion in convertible senior notes set to expire in 2031, with underwriters granted the option to purchase an additional $150 million. Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan Securities, RBC Capital Markets, and Citigroup will be serving as joint managers of the offering.

Some of the proceeds will fund general corporate purposes, including Axon's growth and potential acquisitions or investments, the company said.

Axon has faced broader concerns about disruption by artificial intelligence and a decline in operating income throughout fiscal 2025, and shares have declined 41% over the last 12 months.

While shares dropped Tuesday, Wall Street has held a bullish view on the stock. Of the 23 firms polled by FactSet, Axon stock has an average Buy rating with a price target of $726.56, a 48.2% upside of its Monday closing price of $490.18.

Morgan Stanley analysts wrote Axon's AI offerings presented an opportunity for incremental growth and the potential to expand to more of its services.

Traders praised Axon's expansion into AI services earlier this year after it unveiled AI tools to help police officers generate reports. The company disclosed a 700% surge in subscriptions for its AI tools through its second quarter in August.

In May, the company reported a spike in international sales as its operating income turned positive after five consecutive quarters of losses. President Josh Isner said Axon was "showing up more of a global company at this point" as its non-U.S. business accounted for one-fifth of its total revenue.

data.title: Skyworks Solutions Stock Snaps Back From AI Selloff to Lead the S&P 500 — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Kit Norton

The artificial-intelligence trade selloff couldn't keep Skyworks Solutions stock down for long as it stormed back on Tuesday.

Skyworks Solutions stock rose 11% to $87.92 on Tuesday and was the best-performing stock in the S&P 500 after falling more than 10% on Monday as widespread AI worries hit the stock market.

It didn't take long for investors to pile back into the stock, which advanced 19% last week and was up 31% this month as of last check on Tuesday.

The stock's recent surge accelerated after Skyworks Solutions CEO Philip Brace on Thursday spoke at the Goldman Sachs communications and technology conference.

Brace said he was "very confident" that the pending merger with Qorvo will close "this calendar year" and that the companies are "preparing to close this fiscal year."

That would place the closing at the end of September or in early October.

Investors have been focused on the merger between Skyworks and Qorvo and view it as a massive shift for the analog and mixed-signal semiconductors industry.

The two companies agreed last year to merge in a cash-and-stock deal that marries two of the primary suppliers for components in Apple's iPhones, and creates a $22 billion U.S.-based radio frequency, or RF, analog and mixed-signal semiconductor enterprise.

"I really think this is a transformative deal for both the company and the industry," Brace said last week.

The CEO added that along with the new company's strong mobile business, it will have "super attractive" business opportunities in aerospace and defense for its products.

Along with Skyworks, Qorvo stock rose 7.2% to $115.79 on Tuesday after ending Monday down 7.4%. Similar to Skyworks, Qorvo stock gained 13% last week and has risen 21% in September.

Even with recent performance of Skyworks stock, shares remained down 56% from their record closing high of $199.66 on April 26, 2021. The stock, however, has risen 39% this year and has gained 18% over the past 12 months.

data.title: Bitcoin, crypto stocks slip as hopes for Clarity Act progress fade
data.description:
Bitcoin fell as much as 4.9% on Tuesday from Monday's high of nearly $80K after a Democratic counteroffer over the Clarity Act dimmed hopes of the digital asset legislation progressing.

The price of the largest cryptocurrency by market cap slid to $76.6K Tuesday afternoon, down 3.0% over the past 24 hours. The low of the day was $75.7K, compared with Monday's high-level mark of $79.6K.

Ethereum , the second-largest digital token by market cap, dropped 3.9% to $2.44K.

The odds of the Clarity Act becoming law before Jan. 1, 2027, slid to 13% from as high as 39% at 7:27 AM ET. Legislators have been squabbling over the stablecoin legislation for about a year.

A procedural vote to advance the bill to the Senate floor for a full vote is due to take place Tuesday afternoon. Major sticking points included ethics over legislators and the president profiting from stablecoins and other digital assets and whether platforms should be allowed to pay interest on stablecoin holdings.

Cryptocurrencies and crypto stocks climbed on Monday after Republicans' final draft of the legislation included some ethics restrictions on conflicts of interest. It would also give the Treasury Department authority to intervene if deposit flight started to hurt community banks, according to media reports.

The Federal Reserve's rate decision, to be announced on Wednesday, may also have investors wary of risk assets, including crypto. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee is widely expected to increase its policy rate by 25 basis points, its first hike since 2023.

Crypto stocks slumping the most in Tuesday trading include Circle Internet -11%, Coinbase Global -9.2%, Gemini Space Station -8.6%, and Bakkt -7.1%. Crypto mining stocks also dipped: Riot Platforms -5.9%, CleanSpark -5.6%, Core Scientific -4.8%, Hut 8 -4.4%, and IREN -4.4%.

data.title: Vertiseit establishes global framework agreement with Circle K
data.description:
Visual Art, a company within the Vertiseit Group, has entered into a global framework agreement with Circle K Procurement and Brands Limited regarding the delivery of Digital In-store solutions to Circle K’s operations.

The agreement covers the delivery of a software platform, concept and communications for Circle K’s service stations. The framework agreement is valid until 31 October 2028.

Visual Art has collaborated with Circle K in the Nordic region for approximately ten years. The collaboration has expanded to include new markets in Europe and, more recently, expansion into the North American market.

The framework agreement contains no volume guarantees but represents an opportunity to extend the existing concept to all of Circle K’s service stations globally. Circle K has approximately 14,000 stations, of which the existing delivery currently covers approximately 2,500 stations.

“For us, the agreement is a recognition of our long-term strategic collaboration with Circle K. At the same time, it marks an important step in Visual Art’s development from being a European leader in QSR and Convenience to becoming an established global player,” says Pontus Meijer, CEO of Visual Art.

data.title: Some physical oil cargoes top $130 a barrel, nearing April's record, on Saudi disruptions
data.description:
By Robert Harvey

Prices for some physical oil cargoes in Europe have jumped to more than $130 a barrel on Tuesday, approaching record highs reached in April, as buyers rush to find alternatives to Middle East supplies facing increasing disruptions from intensifying conflict in the region.

Adding to disruptions linked to the Iran war, Saudi Arabia has cancelled late-September cargoes to European buyers after an attack on its East-West Pipeline last week forced it to suspend loadings from key Red Sea port of Yanbu, trade sources said.

Buyers on Tuesday were bidding the price of potential alternatives such as North Sea oil higher. North Sea Forties crude (FOT-E) jumped to a price of $136.75 a barrel, according to LSEG data, approaching the all-time high of $147.37 hit on April 13 soon after the Iran war disrupted Middle East exports.

Oil futures prices rose by over $3 on Tuesday, with the Brent futures contract approaching $110 a barrel, on the Saudi loadings suspension and after Libya halted operations at three oil fields, heightening concerns that disruptions to supply routes could persist for weeks.

The price of physical cargoes is higher than that of crude futures such as Brent in part because the physical cargoes are for delivery in a few weeks, earlier than the oil traded in futures markets. The nearby Brent futures contract is for November delivery.

data.title: Health Rounds: New dye for MRI exams detects lung cancer earlier
data.description:
By Nancy Lapid

Hello Health Rounds readers! Today we highlight a potentially game-changing experimental contrast agent for MRI exams that may enable detection of lung cancer when tumors are small and more treatment options are available. We also report on a Johnson & Johnson antidepressant that appears to help improve sexual dysfunction in patients with major depressive disorder.

New contrast agent finds tiny lung tumors on MRI

A new type of dye for magnetic resonance imaging procedures may let doctors diagnose lung cancer at much earlier stages than is currently possible, researchers found.

In animal studies, the protein-based contrast agent called hProCA32.Collagen2, under development by InLighta BioSciences, allowed for identification of lung tumors and metastases as small as 1 millimeter, according to a report in Science Advances.

"Lung cancer is often diagnosed only after it has spread, when treatment options become more limited," study leader Janny Yang, InLighta's founder and chief scientific officer, said in a statement.

"Our technology can detect tiny tumors and hidden metastases without exposing patients to radiation. It also helps reveal how aggressive a cancer may be and how likely it is to spread, potentially reducing the need for invasive biopsies," Yang added.

The imaging agent hProCA32.Collagen2 targets a structural protein called collagen type I that is found at elevated levels in aggressive lung tumors and metastatic lesions.

Beyond diagnosis, the findings may have important implications for personalized cancer treatment, the researchers said.

By enabling physicians to see collagen remodeling in which old or damaged collagen fibers are broken down and replaced with newly organized proteins in the tumors, the technology may eventually help identify high-risk patients, guide treatment selection and monitor response to therapy over time, they said.

"This is a game changer for cancer diagnosis and precision medicine," said Yang. "For the first time, we've shown that precision MRI can detect tiny tumors and whole-body metastases without using harmful radiation while also providing important clues about how aggressively a cancer may behave."

J&J drug improves depression-related sexual dysfunction

Johnson & Johnson’s antidepressant Caplyta significantly improved sexual dysfunction in a late-stage trial of patients with major depressive disorder that wasn't improving with standard treatment.

In general, antidepressant medications can contribute to sexual dysfunction, making side effects a leading reason patients stop treatment, the study authors said.

More than 80% of the 480 participants in the trial reported sexual dysfunction at the start, according to a report in The Journal of Clinical Psychiatry.

Based on responses to questionnaires, significant improvements in sexual dysfunction were seen in those who were randomly assigned to add a daily 42-milligram dose of Caplyta to their current antidepressant therapy, compared with patients who added a placebo.

The improvements were seen in younger and older adults as well as across various aspects of sexual functioning, such as desire, arousal, orgasm and pleasure.

No changes in sexual function were seen in patients without baseline sexual dysfunction.

Caplyta, known chemically as lumateperone, is already commercially available to treat schizophrenia, bipolar depression and as a supplemental treatment when other antidepressants fail to control major depressive disorder.

Because Caplyta is not associated with medication-induced sexual dysfunction, it may be preferred by patients who need additional depression medications and who wish to avoid that side effect, study leader Dr. Anita Clayton of University of Virginia Health said in a statement.
